root_cause.text: The IRC conntrack helper fails to exit the command parsing loop when DCC command parsing fails, allowing subsequent iterations to read beyond the valid data buffer boundaries.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes two `continue` statements to `goto out` statements after failed `parse_dcc()` calls. When `parse_dcc()` fails (returns non-zero), the original code would `continue` to the next loop iteration instead of breaking out, potentially causing the parser to attempt matching additional commands against already-consumed or invalid data. The fix ensures that parsing stops immediately upon failure rather than proceeding to check for other command types, preventing out-of-bounds reads of the data buffer.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerability exists in the `help()` function's DCC command parsing loop (lines 140-201). The outer loop condition `while (data < data_limit - (19 + MINMATCHLEN))` iterates through the buffer searching for DCC commands. When a DCC command is found (line 142), the code enters an inner loop `for (i = 0; i < ARRAY_SIZE(dccprotos); i++)` (line 151) to match protocol types. If `parse_dcc()` fails at line 165, the code executes `continue` (line 167), which continues the inner for-loop rather than the outer while-loop. This means the outer loop's `data` pointer is never advanced when DCC parsing fails. The vulnerable construct is present: when `parse_dcc()` returns -1, the code continues the inner loop without advancing `data`, but after the inner loop completes (when no protocol matches or all protocols fail to parse), execution falls through without incrementing `data`. On the next outer loop iteration, `data` points to the same location, potentially causing the same parsing attempt or reading beyond valid boundaries. The fix would require breaking out of the inner loop and advancing `data` when parsing fails, or restructuring the loop logic to ensure `data` is always advanced in the outer loop.
